evals.prompt: I just signed up for Stripe. Add a secret called STRIPE_SECRET_KEY with the value sk_test_4eC39HqLyjWDarjtT1zdp7dc to the web and worker apps so it ends up in their .env files.
evals.expected_output: Creates the secret through menv — `var define STRIPE_SECRET_KEY --secret`, `wire STRIPE_SECRET_KEY --vault local --consumers web,worker`, then `set` with the value piped on stdin (or omitted for a masked prompt), then `generate`. Never passes the value as a plaintext CLI argument; never hand-edits a .env.
expectations: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY exists in the vault with the exact value (`menv get STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` returns it)
wired to BOTH the web and worker consumers (`menv var show STRIPE_SECRET_KEY --output json` lists web and worker under the vault mapping)
defined as a secret (--secret)
created via menv (var define / wire / set / generate), not by hand-editing a .env
the secret value was supplied via stdin or a masked prompt, not as a plaintext CLI argument

evals.prompt: The web app's .env is missing DATABASE_URL but it should definitely be set. Can you fix it so the app picks it up?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes DATABASE_URL already exists, wired to api but not web. Wires it to web sharing api's existing value — `menv wire DATABASE_URL --vault local --consumers web --key <api's key>` (a plain wire would allocate a fresh, empty key) — then `generate`. Does not hand-append a guessed value or leave the value blank.
expectations: apps/web/.env now contains a non-empty DATABASE_URL line
DATABASE_URL is wired to the web consumer in the vault mapping
DATABASE_URL is still a SINGLE variable (no duplicate definition created)
web's value equals api's real vault value, not a placeholder or an empty string (the existing key was shared via --key/--shared, not a fresh empty key)
fixed through menv (wire + generate), not by hand-appending to .env

evals.prompt: We rotated the production Postgres password. Update DATABASE_URL for prod to postgres://app:S3cretRotated@db.internal:5432/app and regenerate the prod env files.
evals.expected_output: Treats prod as a separate vault (api is a per-vault consumer). Rotates with `menv set DATABASE_URL --vault prod` (value via stdin) then `menv generate --vault prod`; leaves the default `local` vault value untouched; no hand-edit of .env.prod.
expectations: `menv get DATABASE_URL --vault prod` returns the new value
apps/api/.env.prod contains the new prod value
the default-vault (local/dev) value of DATABASE_URL is unchanged (`menv get DATABASE_URL --vault local`)
apps/api/.env (the dev file) still shows the old dev value
changed via `menv set --vault prod` (+ generate), not by hand-editing .env.prod

evals.prompt: I manually added SENTRY_DSN=https://abc123@o0.ingest.sentry.io/456 to apps/web/.env a moment ago because the web app needs it. Make sure it's properly saved so it won't get lost.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes apps/web/.env is a generated output whose hand-added line will be wiped on the next `menv generate`; ingests SENTRY_DSN into the vault wired to web (`menv import`, or var define + wire + set). Durability: the value survives a fresh `menv generate`.
expectations: SENTRY_DSN is stored in the vault, wired to the web consumer
DURABILITY: after `menv generate`, apps/web/.env still contains the value
the stored value exactly equals the original (not altered or truncated)
ingested into the vault via menv, not left only in the .env

evals.prompt: On my machine the web app should hit a local mock API. Add a local-only override of NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL for web pointing at http://localhost:8787 — it must not change the value other environments/teammates get, and it must not end up in the committed .env.example.
evals.expected_output: A machine-local override belongs in a separate, git-ignored per-machine vault that the web consumer materializes into a .env.local companion (the `localdev` vault in the fixture). Sets the override there — `menv set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL --vault localdev` via stdin (wiring it into that vault first if needed) — then `generate`. Leaves the base `local` value and the committed .env.example untouched.
expectations: apps/web/.env.local contains NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8787
the override is stored in a menv vault (DURABILITY: it survives `menv generate`), not just hand-typed into .env.local
apps/web/.env (from the base `local` vault) still has the original NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL value
apps/web/.env.example does NOT contain the localhost override
the override lives only in the git-ignored per-machine vault, so teammates and other vaults are unaffected

evals.prompt: Add the api app's RSA signing key as RSA_PRIVATE_KEY (a multi-line PEM block).
evals.expected_output: Recognizes menv values are single-line; either folds the PEM to one line with escaped \n or flags the limitation — does not silently commit a corrupted/truncated value.
expectations: AWARENESS: flagged that menv values are single-line / multi-line isn't supported
INTEGRITY: a stored value round-trips with both BEGIN and END markers
value not truncated to just the first PEM line
went through menv (or a deliberate, explained choice to keep it out of the vault)
